column1: # Which decks compare their transient output against the Xyce reference row by
# row, and which fall back to interpolation.
# The Xyce suite has two transient comparison geometries and picks between them
# per deck, from the two time axes alone:
#   index_aligned   Reference row i is compared against accepted step i of the
#                   run. Chosen when the run produced exactly as many samples
#                   as the reference has rows AND no adjacent interval drifts
#                   outside the ratio window [0.75, 4/3]. This is the strictest
#                   claim the suite makes about a transient: the engine had to
#                   choose essentially the same steps Xyce chose.
#   interpolated    The run is evaluated at each reference time instead. A
#                   materially weaker claim -- the waveform passes through the
#                   right points, with nothing said about where the integrator
# Nothing declares the mode. It is derived, so a change to the engine's
# accepted-step sequence can move a deck from the strict geometry to the
# lenient one with no edit to the deck, its tolerances, or its contract, and
# every test still passes while the gate quietly weakens. That is the failure
# this file exists to make impossible.
# Every row below names a deck that currently compares index-aligned. The
# `xyce_regression` suite enforces the list in BOTH directions:
#   * a manifested deck that falls back to interpolation, or that stops
#     reaching a transient comparison at all, FAILS; and
#   * an unmanifested deck that starts comparing index-aligned FAILS too, so
#     the list cannot rot into a description of a corpus that moved on.
# Rows are `<relative path under tests/xyce>` TAB `index_aligned`, sorted by
# path, one deck per row. `index_aligned` is the only legal mode: a deck that
# interpolates is recorded by its absence.
# Capture a fresh census, which is written before the suite's own assertions so
# that a run this manifest fails still produces one:
# The report lists every deck that reached a transient comparison with the mode
# it used. Copy its `index_aligned` rows in below this header, then re-run to
# Record in the commit message which engine change moved the grid and why the
# weaker comparison is acceptable for every deck that lost the strict one. A
# manifest regenerated without that judgement is a gate that has been switched
# off rather than one that has been updated.
